instruction_bn: সংকেত অনুসরণ করে গল্পটি সম্পূর্ণ করো এবং একটি উপযুক্ত শিরোনাম ও নীতিকথা (moral) দাও। নিজে লেখার পর নমুনা ও checklist দেখো (Board: 15 marks)।

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A greedy dog — got a piece of meat — crossed a bridge — saw its shadow in water — thought it another dog with meat — barked to snatch it — lost its own meat.
items.model:
The Greedy Dog

Once a dog was very hungry. It searched here and there for food. At last it found a piece of meat in a butcher's shop. It took the meat in its mouth and ran to a lonely place to eat it. On the way it had to cross a narrow bridge over a river. As it was crossing the bridge, it looked down and saw its own shadow in the water. The foolish dog thought that it was another dog with a piece of meat. It became greedy and wanted to snatch that piece too. So it barked at the shadow with its mouth open. As soon as it opened its mouth, its own piece of meat fell into the water and was lost for ever. The greedy dog now repented, but it was too late.

Moral: Grasp all, lose all.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A crow — stole a piece of cheese — sat on a tree — a hungry fox saw it — praised the crow's voice — asked it to sing — the crow began to sing — cheese fell down — fox took it.
items.model:
The Fox and the Crow

Once a crow stole a piece of cheese from a window. It flew up and sat on the branch of a tree to eat it. Just then a hungry fox was passing by. It saw the cheese in the crow's beak and wanted to get it. The fox was very cunning. It came under the tree and began to praise the crow. 'What a beautiful bird you are!' it said. 'Your voice must be as sweet as your looks. Please sing a song for me.' The foolish crow was pleased at this flattery. To show its sweet voice, it opened its beak to sing. At once the piece of cheese fell down from its beak. The clever fox caught it and ran away, laughing at the foolish crow.

Moral: Beware of flatterers.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: An old man — had four lazy sons — before death — told them a treasure was hidden in the field — after his death — sons dug the field — found no treasure — but got a good harvest.
items.model:
The Hidden Treasure

Once there lived an old farmer in a village. He had four sons who were very lazy. They never worked and always quarrelled among themselves. The old man was very worried about their future. When he was about to die, he called his sons to his bedside. He told them that he had hidden a treasure somewhere in his field. After his death the sons wanted to get the treasure quickly. They took spades and dug the whole field very carefully. But they found no treasure anywhere. They were disappointed. As the field had been dug well, one of them advised sowing seeds in it. They did so. In time the field gave them a rich harvest. Then they understood the real meaning of their father's words.

Moral: Industry is the key to success.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A hare — proud of its speed — made fun of a tortoise — the tortoise challenged it to a race — the hare ran fast then slept — the tortoise walked on slowly — reached the goal first.
items.model:
The Hare and the Tortoise

Once there lived a hare and a tortoise in a forest. The hare was very proud of its speed. It often made fun of the tortoise for its slow movement. One day the tortoise felt hurt and challenged the hare to a race. The hare laughed and agreed. The race began. The hare ran very fast and soon left the tortoise far behind. Feeling sure of its victory, the hare thought of taking a short rest. It lay down under a tree and soon fell asleep. Meanwhile the tortoise kept walking slowly but steadily. It passed the sleeping hare and reached the goal. When the hare woke up and ran to the goal, it found that the tortoise had already won the race. The hare was ashamed of its pride.

Moral: Slow and steady wins the race.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A fox — was very hungry — saw ripe grapes on a high vine — jumped again and again — could not reach them — went away saying the grapes were sour.
items.model:
The Fox and the Grapes

One hot summer day a fox was walking through a garden. It was very hungry and was looking for food. Suddenly it saw a bunch of ripe grapes hanging from a high vine. The grapes looked juicy and sweet. The fox's mouth watered at the sight. It wanted to eat the grapes at any cost. So it jumped up to reach them, but it failed. It jumped again and again with all its might, yet it could not reach the grapes, for they were too high. At last the fox became tired and gave up trying. But it did not want to admit its failure. So, walking away, it said to itself, 'The grapes are sour. They are not worth eating.'

Moral: The grapes are sour to those who cannot reach them.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: An old man — a bundle of sticks — his sons always quarrelled — asked each to break the whole bundle — none could — then broke the sticks one by one easily — taught them unity.
items.model:
Unity Is Strength

Once there lived an old man in a village. He had several sons. They loved one another, but they often quarrelled among themselves. The old man was very unhappy to see this. He wanted to teach them the value of unity. One day he called all his sons and gave them a bundle of sticks. He asked each of them to break the whole bundle. One by one they tried their best, but none of them could break it. Then the old man untied the bundle and gave each son a single stick. He asked them to break it. This time each of them broke the stick very easily. The old man said, 'If you remain united like the bundle, no one can harm you. But if you are divided, your enemies will break you easily.' The sons understood the lesson.

Moral: Unity is strength.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A poor woodcutter — his axe fell into a river — began to weep — a fairy appeared — showed a gold and a silver axe — he refused them — took only his iron axe — the fairy gave him all three for his honesty.
items.model:
The Honest Woodcutter

Once there lived a poor woodcutter. He earned his living by cutting wood in a forest near a river. One day he was cutting a tree on the bank of the river. Suddenly his axe slipped from his hand and fell into the deep water. He had no other axe, so he sat on the bank and began to weep. At this a water fairy appeared before him. She dived into the water and brought up a golden axe. She asked if it was his. The honest woodcutter said, 'No.' Then she brought up a silver axe, but again he said it was not his. At last she brought up his own iron axe. The woodcutter cried out with joy, 'Yes, this is my axe.' The fairy was pleased with his honesty and gave him all three axes as a reward.

Moral: Honesty is the best policy.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A fox — fell into a well — could not get out — a thirsty goat came — the fox praised the water — the goat jumped in — the fox climbed out on the goat's back — left the goat in the well.
items.model:
The Fox and the Goat

Once a fox fell into a deep well. The water in it was low, so the fox did not drown, but it could not get out anyhow. It tried again and again, yet it failed. After some time a thirsty goat came to the well in search of water. It saw the fox inside and asked whether the water was good. The cunning fox hid its trouble and said, 'The water is very sweet and cool. Come down and drink to your heart's content.' The foolish goat believed the fox and at once jumped into the well. When the goat had drunk enough, the fox said, 'Let us think how to get out.' Then the clever fox climbed up on the goat's back and jumped out of the well. It left the poor goat inside and ran away.

Moral: Look before you leap.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: King Bruce — defeated many times — hid in a cave — saw a spider trying to reach the ceiling — it failed six times — succeeded the seventh time — the king took heart and won.
items.model:
Try Again

Robert Bruce was the king of Scotland. He fought many battles against the English to free his country. But he was defeated again and again. At last he lost all hope and hid himself in a lonely cave. One day, as he was lying in the cave, he saw a spider trying to reach the ceiling by its web. The spider tried to climb up but fell down. It tried a second time, a third time and so on, but each time it failed. Bruce counted that the spider had failed six times. Yet it did not give up. On the seventh try, the spider at last reached the ceiling. This sight gave Bruce new hope and courage. He came out of the cave, gathered his soldiers again and fought against the enemy. This time he defeated them and freed his country.

Moral: If at first you don't succeed, try, try again.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: Two friends — passing through a forest — a bear came — one climbed a tree — the other lay down like dead — the bear smelt him and went away — the friend on the tree asked what the bear said.
items.model:
A Friend in Need

Once two friends were passing through a forest. They had promised to help each other in times of danger. Suddenly a big bear appeared before them. One of the friends was selfish. He at once climbed up a tree to save himself, without thinking of his friend. The other friend did not know how to climb. He was in great danger. But he had heard that a bear does not touch a dead body. So he lay down on the ground and held his breath like a dead man. The bear came near him and smelt his ears and nose. Taking him for dead, it went away. Then the first friend came down and asked what the bear had whispered in his ear. The other replied, 'The bear has told me not to trust a selfish friend.'

Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A shepherd boy — used to cry 'Wolf! Wolf!' for fun — villagers came running — found no wolf — one day a real wolf came — the boy cried for help — nobody believed him — the wolf killed the sheep.
items.model:
The Shepherd Boy and the Wolf

Once there was a shepherd boy in a village. Every day he took his sheep to a field to graze. The field was far from the village, and the boy often felt lonely and bored. One day, just for fun, he cried out loudly, 'Wolf! Wolf!' Hearing his cry, the villagers ran to the field with sticks to save the sheep. But they found no wolf and returned home angrily. The boy laughed at them. He played the same trick a few more times, and each time the villagers were fooled. A few days later a real wolf attacked the flock. The frightened boy cried out, 'Wolf! Wolf!' with all his might. But this time the villagers thought it was another false alarm, so nobody came to help him. The wolf killed and ate many of his sheep.

Moral: A liar is not believed even when he tells the truth.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A thirsty crow — found a jar with little water — could not reach it — dropped pebbles one by one — the water rose up — drank and flew away.
items.model:
The Thirsty Crow

One hot summer day a crow felt very thirsty. It flew here and there in search of water, but it could not find any. At last it saw a jar in a garden. The crow flew down to the jar and found a little water at the bottom. But the water was so low that it could not reach it with its beak. It tried again and again but failed. The crow did not lose heart. Suddenly a clever plan came to its mind. It saw some small pebbles lying nearby. The crow began to drop the pebbles into the jar one by one. As the pebbles went in, the water slowly rose up. When the water came near the mouth of the jar, the crow drank it to its heart's content. Then it flew away happily.

Moral: Where there is a will, there is a way.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A camel — asked a jackal to help find food — they went to a field — the camel ate crops — the jackal howled — villagers came and beat the camel — the camel took revenge.
items.model:
The Camel and the Jackal

Once a camel and a jackal were friends. One day the jackal said, 'I know a field full of sweet crops across the river. Let us go there.' The camel agreed and carried the jackal across the river on its back. They reached the field and began to eat. The jackal soon finished its little meal, but the camel was still eating. Then the jackal started to howl loudly. Hearing the howl, the villagers came running with sticks and beat the poor camel badly. When they left, the camel asked the jackal why it had howled so early. The jackal cleverly replied that it had a habit of howling after a meal. On the way back, the camel took the jackal on its back. In the middle of the river the camel dived into the water, and the jackal was washed away.

Moral: Tit for tat.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: An ant — fell into water — a dove dropped a leaf — the ant climbed on it and was saved — later a hunter aimed at the dove — the ant bit his foot — the dove flew away.
items.model:
The Ant and the Dove

Once an ant went to a river to drink water. While drinking, it slipped and fell into the water. The current began to carry it away, and the ant struggled hard for its life. A dove was sitting on a tree by the river. Seeing the danger of the ant, the kind dove plucked a leaf and dropped it near the ant. The ant quickly climbed onto the leaf and floated to the bank. Thus its life was saved. A few days later a hunter came to the river. He saw the dove sitting on the tree and aimed his gun at it. The ant noticed this and wanted to save its friend. It quickly crawled up and bit the hunter hard on the foot. The hunter cried out in pain, and his gun missed the aim. At once the dove flew away and saved its life.

Moral: One good turn deserves another.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A lion — sleeping in a forest — a mouse ran over its body — the lion caught it — the mouse begged for mercy — the lion let it go — later the lion was trapped in a net — the mouse cut the net and saved it.
items.model:
The Lion and the Mouse

Once a lion was sleeping in a forest. A little mouse was playing nearby. By chance it ran over the body of the lion. The lion woke up in anger and caught the mouse in its paw. The frightened mouse begged for mercy. It said, 'Please forgive me this time, sir. If you set me free, I may help you some day.' The lion laughed at the idea that such a tiny creature could help him. But he took pity on the mouse and let it go. Some days later the lion was caught in a hunter's net. It roared loudly but could not free itself. The mouse heard the roar and came running. It cut the net with its sharp teeth and set the lion free. The lion was grateful to the little mouse.

Moral: Do not hate anyone as weak or small.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A farmer — had a goose — it laid a golden egg every day — the greedy farmer wanted all the eggs at once — killed the goose — found nothing inside — lost everything.
items.model:
The Goose That Laid Golden Eggs

Once a farmer had a wonderful goose. Every morning the goose laid a golden egg. The farmer sold the eggs in the market and slowly became rich. But he was very greedy. He was not satisfied with one egg a day. He thought that there must be a heap of gold inside the goose. He wanted to get all the gold at once. So one day he killed the goose and cut open its body to take out the gold. But to his surprise, he found nothing inside. It was just like any other goose. Now he had neither the gold nor the golden eggs. His greed had ruined him completely. He repented for his foolishness, but it was too late.

Moral: Greed is a curse.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A milkmaid — carrying a pot of milk on her head — dreaming of profit — planning to buy eggs, chickens and a dress — nodded her head in joy — the pot fell down — all her dreams were broken.
items.model:
Do Not Count Your Chickens Before They Are Hatched

Once a milkmaid was going to the market to sell a pot of milk. She was carrying the pot on her head. As she walked along, she began to build castles in the air. She thought, 'With the money from this milk, I shall buy some eggs. The eggs will give me chickens. I shall sell the chickens and buy a beautiful dress. Wearing that dress, I shall go to the fair. Many young men will look at me, but I shall proudly toss my head and refuse them all.' Thinking this, she really tossed her head in joy. At once the pot of milk fell down from her head and broke. All the milk was spilt on the ground. With the milk, all her sweet dreams were also broken.

Moral: Do not build castles in the air.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A cap seller — slept under a tree — a group of monkeys took his caps — he woke up and saw them wearing caps — he threw his own cap down in anger — the monkeys copied him — he got back all his caps.
items.model:
The Cap Seller and the Monkeys

Once there was a cap seller. He used to sell caps from village to village. One hot afternoon he felt very tired. He put down his basket of caps and lay down under a big tree to take rest. Soon he fell fast asleep. There were many monkeys on the tree. They came down, took the caps from the basket and put them on their heads. Then they climbed up the tree again. When the cap seller woke up, he found his basket empty. Looking up, he saw the monkeys wearing his caps. He shouted and made faces at them, but the monkeys only imitated him. At last, in anger, he threw his own cap on the ground. At once the monkeys also threw down their caps in imitation. The clever cap seller quickly gathered all his caps and went away happily.

Moral: Wisdom wins where force fails.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: The sun and the wind — quarrelled about who was stronger — a traveller came — they agreed to test on him — the wind blew hard but the man held his coat tight — the sun shone warmly — the man took off his coat — the sun won.
items.model:
The Sun and the Wind

Once the sun and the wind had a quarrel. Each of them claimed to be stronger than the other. Just then they saw a traveller walking along the road with a coat on. They agreed that the one who could make the traveller take off his coat would be the stronger. First the wind took its turn. It began to blow very hard and cold. But the harder the wind blew, the more tightly the traveller wrapped his coat around him. At last the wind gave up. Then it was the sun's turn. The sun came out and began to shine gently and warmly. Slowly the day grew hot. The traveller began to sweat. Feeling too hot, he took off his coat at once. Thus the sun won the contest.

Moral: Gentleness can do what force cannot.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: Bayazid Bostami — his mother felt thirsty at night — asked for water — he brought water — she had fallen asleep — he stood by her bed holding the glass all night.
items.model:
A Devoted Son

Bayazid Bostami was a great Muslim saint. He loved and served his mother very much. One night his mother fell ill and felt very thirsty. She asked Bayazid for a glass of water. Bayazid at once went to fetch water. But when he came back with the water, he found that his mother had fallen asleep. He did not want to wake her from her sleep. So he stood silently by her bed, holding the glass of water in his hand. He waited there patiently for his mother to wake up. In this way he passed the whole night standing without any rest. When his mother woke up in the early morning, she was greatly moved to see her devoted son. She gave him her heartfelt blessings.

Moral: Service to mother is a great virtue.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A donkey — put on a lion's skin — frightened all the animals — brayed loudly out of pride — the fox knew it by its voice — the donkey was caught and beaten.
items.model:
The Donkey in the Lion's Skin

Once a donkey found the skin of a dead lion in a forest. A foolish idea came into its mind. It put on the lion's skin and began to move about in the forest. Seeing the shape of a lion, all the animals ran away in fear. The donkey was very pleased to see this. It enjoyed frightening the other animals for some days. It became very proud of itself. One day, out of pride, it began to bray loudly. A clever fox was passing by. As soon as it heard the sound, it understood that it was only a donkey and not a lion. The fox said, 'I would have been afraid too, if I had not heard your voice.' Soon the other animals also came to know the truth. They caught the donkey and gave it a good beating.

Moral: Pride goes before a fall.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে
